battle.name: 西班牙立憲革命
battle.brief: 一八二〇年元旦，炮兵上尉列戈在加的斯宣布擁護一八一二年《加的斯憲法》，數週內全國倒戈，國王三月九日宣誓，制憲議會七月重開。一八二三年法軍越比達索阿河入伊，五月二十三日占領馬德里，自由三年期終結，列戈十一月被槍斃。火繩槍此時已屬舊式火器，僅見於民兵與軍械庫，線列步兵實用燧發槍。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 這場戰爭是西班牙王國在波旁王朝復辟之後的一場內戰兼革命，一八二〇年至一八二三年的「自由三年期」由三股政治軍力角力構成。第一股是國王斐迪南七世與其身旁的「使徒派」王黨，包括樞密院、宮廷侍從、若干線列軍團與近衛軍團，以及一八二二年起在各省成立的「王黨志願兵」武裝；第二股是自由派，即主張恢復一八一二年《加的斯憲法》的議員、將軍與文官，起義初期依靠軍隊中願意pronunciamiento（西班牙語「宣告效忠」）的軍官、地方執政會議與城鎮民兵；第三股是外來干涉力量，一八二三年法國波旁王朝以「聖路易十字軍」之名出兵十萬眾，用以把斐迪南七世從自由派手中「拯救」回來。此役的指揮系統極為分散：自由派沒有統一司令部，各地地方執政會議以民選代表與軍官混合組成，逐處決定是否加入革命；國王一方則由樞密院與御前會議調度，分派王命；法軍則有明確的遠征指揮官與連續作戰的分遣縱隊。整場衝突的勝負，多數時候並非由戰場上的火力決定，而是由哪一方的軍官願意在關鍵節點倒戈決定。火繩槍作為一八二〇年代西班牙民間武裝與二線守備仍可能取用的舊式槍械，其正反面都在這個結構裡被放大。
countriesEn: This war was a civil war and a revolution inside the Kingdom of Spain after the Bourbon restoration, fought across the three years of the Liberal Triennium, 1820 to 1823. Three political-military forces struggled for control. The first was King Ferdinand VII and the absolutist 'apostolic' party around him, together with the privy council, the court camarilla, several line regiments and the Royal Guard, plus the Royalist Volunteers raised in the provinces from 1822. The second was the liberal party, that is the members of the Cortes, the generals and the civil officials who wanted the Constitution of 1812 restored; at the outset they relied on those officers of the army who were willing to pronounce for the Constitution, on the local juntas and on the urban militias. The third was foreign intervention: in 1823 the Bourbon monarchy of France marched in with the Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis, in order to rescue Ferdinand VII from the liberals. The command structure of the campaign was extremely diffuse. The liberals had no single headquarters; the local juntas, mixing elected representatives with officers, decided town by town whether to join the rising. The royal side was coordinated by the privy council and the royal cabinet, which dispatched royal orders. The French army, by contrast, had a clear expeditionary command and columns operating in succession. For most of the conflict the outcome was decided not by firepower on the field but by which officers were willing to defect at the critical moment. The matchlock, the weapon shown on the card, is an old arm that the improvised militias and the second-line garrisons of the 1820s could still draw on, and both its strengths and its weaknesses were magnified by this structure.
people: 領袖人物方面，起義的引爆點是陸軍炮兵上尉拉斐爾·德·列戈（Rafael del Riego）。一八一九年十二月底，他駐紮在加的斯，籍由炮兵軍官之間的普遍不滿，以及對政府干預軍官榮譽、晉升與宮廷人事的反感，於除夕夜率領駐軍離開營門，連夜向加的斯市民宣布擁護一八一二年《加的斯憲法》；消息在十天之內傳遍安達盧西亞，馬德里、塞維亞、巴塞羅那等城市的駐軍與地方議會相繼表態，整個半島在數週內倒向國王。斐迪南七世本人在三月被迫宣誓接受憲法，隨後企圖以拖延、遷都與改組內閣來逆轉潮流，最終在自由派控制的軍隊與國民警衛隊面前節節退讓。一八二一年後，王后瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜以攝政身分主持「急攝政」與「三年攝政」，是自由派在宮廷內最重要的支柱。內閣方面，阿古斯丁·阿爾格萊斯與弗朗西斯科·馬丁內斯·德·拉·羅薩是最有影響力的自由派政治家，前者以演說與辯才著稱，後者在自由派分裂後主持內閣並起草一八二二年《皇家法令》。青年將領弗朗西斯科·哈維爾·德·托里霍斯與巴洛梅羅·埃斯帕特羅分別在南部與北部打游擊；一八二三年抵抗法軍最力的埃斯帕特羅在納瓦拉攻下潘普洛納。一八二三年法軍方面的指揮官是法國波旁使節昂古萊公爵，部隊由德羅埃·德·埃爾隆元帥率領，爾隆的前鋒在邊境實施強行渡河。介入的代價落在列戈自己身上：同年十一月，他以「擅自發動軍事政變」之罪被押上刑場，槍斃處決。
peopleEn: As for the leading figures, the spark of the rising was Rafael del Riego, a captain in the army artillery. At the end of December 1819, while stationed at Cadiz, he acted on the widespread resentment of the artillery officer corps, and on their anger at government interference with their honour, their promotion and court appointments. On the night of New Year's Eve he marched the garrison out of its barracks and proclaimed to the citizens of Cadiz his support for the Constitution of 1812. Within ten days the news had spread through Andalusia; the garrisons and the local councils of Madrid, Seville, Barcelona and other cities declared in turn, and inside a few weeks the whole peninsula had turned against the king. Ferdinand VII himself was forced to swear the Constitution in March, and afterwards tried to reverse the tide by delay, by moving the court and by reshuffling the cabinet, yielding step by step to the constitutionalist army and the National Guard. After 1821 Queen Maria Cristina, acting as regent, headed the Urgency Regency and then the Triennial Regency, and was the most important pillar of the liberal cause inside the palace. On the cabinet side, Agustin Arguelles and Francisco Martinez de la Rosa were the most influential liberal politicians: the former was famed for his oratory, the latter led the government after the liberal split and drafted the Royal Statute of 1822. The young officers Francisco Javier de Torrijos and Baldomero Espartero fought as guerrillas in the south and the north respectively; in 1823 Espartero, the most stubborn resister of the French, took Pamplona in Navarre. On the French side the expedition was under the Bourbon emissary, the Duke of Angouleme, and the army was led by Marshal Drouet d'Erlon, whose vanguard forced the crossing of the frontier river. The cost of the intervention fell on Riego himself: in November of the same year he was dragged before a firing squad and shot, the charge being precisely that he had started a military pronunciamiento without authority.
kits: 卡面這件火繩槍是十六世紀西班牙軍的標準火器：單管長身，前段有喇叭口，中段設火繩夾與點火桿，後段有扳機與護圈，槍管與木托同軸，用時必須先點起火繩、保持陰燃，再把槍托抵肩瞄準。它在一八二〇年已屬古董：西班牙陸軍線列步兵在一八一九至一八二〇年間已全面改用燧發滑膛步槍，口徑約十三至十四公厘，槍身帶銅飾，槍兵與炮兵同樣以燧發槍為主。火繩槍仍可能出現的地方有三個：一是軍械庫上層的存貨，二是新成立的城市民兵「國民警衛隊」與地方武裝使用的雜式舊槍，三是偏僻守備與要塞內的殘存裝備。在本場衝突的幾個關鍵場面，例如一八二〇年七月馬德里王宮近衛與街壆的對峙，以及一八二三年的城防與街道戰，出現在民眾一方的多數是霰彈槍、手槍與火繩槍這類舊式火器；士兵必須先點火才能射擊，火繩一旦受潮或被風吹熄便完全失效，這也是它在火藥年代被人詬病的地方。與此同時，自由派在正面上所面對的法軍與王室軍線列步兵，使用的仍是燧發槍，配合銅製滑膛砲與騎兵馬刀，並有工兵與攻城器材配合。火繩槍在本場戰爭中的位置因此不是主力交戰兵器，而是革命陣營物資匱乏、國王調空軍械庫之後的替代品。
kitsEn: The matchlock on the card was the standard Spanish army arm of the sixteenth century: a single long barrel with a flared muzzle, a clamp for the match and a serpentine, a lock and a trigger, barrel and wooden stock in one piece. To use it a soldier had to light the match, keep it smouldering, shoulder the weapon and aim. By 1820 it was already an antique. The Spanish line infantry had moved over between 1819 and 1820 to the flintlock smoothbore musket, of a caliber of roughly thirteen to fourteen millimetres, with brass furniture, and the musketeers and the artillery likewise carried flintlocks. The matchlock could still appear in three places: as surplus stock in the upper arsenals, as the mixed old weapons handed to the newly raised urban National Guard and to provincial bands, and as surviving weapons in remote garrisons and fortresses. In the key moments of this conflict, such as the clash between the Royal Guard and the street crowds in Madrid in July 1820 and the street and gate fighting of 1823, the civilian side was armed mostly with shotguns, pistols and old matchlocks; a soldier had to light his match before he could shoot, and if the slow match was damp or blown out the weapon was simply useless, which was a much-cited fault of the gunpowder era. Meanwhile the French and the royal line infantry that the liberals faced in the open still fought with flintlocks, supported by bronze smoothbore guns, cavalry sabres, engineers and siege equipment. The matchlock's place in this war was therefore not that of a main battle arm, but of a substitute handed to the revolutionary camp after the king had drained the arsenals and the liberal side could not be resupplied.
tactics:
本役的戰術可以分兩段來看。前一段是一八二〇年的革命，也就是一連串以行軍與政治表態為主的pronunciamiento式作戰：起義的軍官帶著本營部隊沿大道進城，在城門口宣讀擁護憲法的聲明，控制兵營、軍械庫與要塞，把國王派任的守軍解除武裝，然後把整支隊伍向省會推進。火繩槍在這種局面裡幾乎沒有射擊的機會，真正決定進展的是速度、士氣與奪權的時機；少數流血衝突集中在城市街道與兵營門口，交火雙方往往互不對射，只在遭遇的瞬間打幾輪便各自散開，而火繩槍在這種短兵相接中的遲緩與不可靠，往往比對方的火槍更致命。線列步兵所繼承的密集橫隊與齊射，以及「鼓聲齊射」這類靠鼓點統一射擊的紀律，正是火繩槍時代留下的習慣：火繩槍要點火、要瞄準、要排隊，缺點都被方陣式的橫隊化成整齊的彈幕。
後一段是一八二三年的法軍反攻，才回到正面戰役的樣態。法軍以縱隊行軍，以戰鬥散兵在道路兩側與村落佔領掩體，砲兵集中射擊，用霰彈射程在數百公尺內驅散對方散兵線，再由步兵在掩體掩護下接敵；騎兵負責掩護縱隊側翼與追擊潰兵。西班牙自由派沒有能力與法軍打會戰，多採游擊與地方守備的辦法，在加泰隆尼亞、巴斯克與納瓦拉一帶由志願兵與武裝農民騷擾法軍後方，切斷從法國邊境到馬德里的補給線；埃斯帕特羅在北方以少量正規步兵配合攻城器械拿下潘普洛納等要塞，這已完全是燧發槍與散兵線的戰爭，火繩槍在這一階段更退到背景。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the campaign fall into two halves. The first is the revolution of 1820, a run of pronunciamientos fought with marching and political declaration rather than with set-piece battle. The insurgent officers led their own companies along the main roads into the towns, read out a declaration of support for the Constitution at the city gate, seized the barracks, the arsenals and the fortresses, disarmed the garrisons appointed by the king, and then marched the whole column on the provincial capital. The matchlock had almost no chance to fire in such a situation; what decided the speed of events was momentum, morale and the timing of the seizure of power. The few bloody clashes were concentrated in the city streets and at barracks gates, where the two sides often did not exchange sustained volleys but fired a few rounds on contact and then scattered, and there the sluggishness and unreliability of the matchlock was often more fatal than the enemy's muskets. The dense line and the massed volley inherited by the line infantry, together with the drum-beaten fire discipline, are precisely the habits left over from the matchlock era: the matchlock had to be lit, aimed and ranked, and the square formation turned those weaknesses into an orderly barrage. The second half is the French counter-offensive of 1823, which returns to the pattern of a real campaign. The French marched in column, used skirmishers to hold the roadsides and the shelter of villages, concentrated their artillery, drove the enemy loose lines apart with canister at a few hundred metres, and brought their infantry up under cover; cavalry covered the flanks of the columns and harried the fugitives. The Spanish liberals had no capacity to meet the French in a pitched battle, and fell back on guerrilla war and local defence, with volunteers and armed peasants harassing the French rear in Catalonia, the Basque country and Navarre and cutting the supply line from the French border to Madrid. Espartero in the north reduced fortresses such as Pamplona with a handful of regular infantry and siege equipment. By then the war was entirely one of flintlocks and loose lines, and the matchlock had retreated into the background.
data: 可查證的數字大致如下。立憲派方面，一八二〇年一月一日起義爆發，數週之內全國各地的軍隊與地方議會接連表態，國王在三月九日正式宣誓接受一八一二年《加的斯憲法》；該憲法由加的斯的制憲議會於一八一二年三月七日頒布。同年的制憲議會在七月九日於聖路加爾－德巴拉梅達重新開議，其後遷往塞維亞，再遷往加的斯。一八二二年三月，議會解散，四月三十日頒布《皇家法令》，建立兩院制並給予國王廣泛權力。一八二三年的法國干涉軍，官方宣稱十萬人，通常估計實際入境的兵力約在八萬上下，另有數萬名西班牙王黨志願兵隨法軍作戰；法軍前鋒於四月初越過比達索阿河，五月二十三日進入馬德里。西班牙常備軍的官方編制約十萬人，但實際在營人數遠低於此，且分駐全國各要塞，難以集中；新組建的國民警衛隊與王黨志願兵則按城鎮臨時徵集，裝備與訓練參差齊劣。城防與街道戰的傷亡數字，兩造說法不一，史料多以「雙方均有數十人死傷」概括，具體人數無從考證。火繩槍這類舊式火器沒有留下可核對的發射數或消耗量記錄。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are roughly these. On the constitutionalist side, the rising began on 1 January 1820; within weeks the armies and local councils across the country declared in turn, and the king formally swore the Constitution of 1812 on 9 March, the Constitution having been promulgated on 7 March 1812 by the Constituent Cortes at Cadiz. The Constituent Cortes of that year reopened on 9 July at Sanlucar de Barrameda, later moving to Seville and then to Cadiz. In March 1822 the Cortes was dissolved, and on 30 April the Royal Statute was promulgated, creating a bicameral Cortes and granting the king wide powers. The French army of intervention was officially proclaimed as a hundred thousand men; the force actually brought into Spain is usually estimated at around eighty thousand, with several tens of thousands of Spanish royalist volunteers serving alongside. The French vanguard crossed the Bidassoa in early April and entered Madrid on 23 May. The official establishment of the Spanish army was about a hundred thousand men, but the number actually under arms was far lower, and the regiments were dispersed among the fortresses of the country so that they could not be concentrated; the newly raised National Guard and the royalist volunteers were levied town by town, with equipment and training that varied wildly. Casualty figures for the fighting in the streets and at the gates are given inconsistently by the two sides, and the sources generally summarise them as dozens dead and wounded on both sides; exact numbers cannot be verified. No firing or consumption records survive for the older weapons such as the matchlock.
cause: 直接起因是拿破崙戰爭之後國王斐迪南七世的復辟。戰爭期間的西班牙曾由自由派主導，於一八一二年制定了《加的斯憲法》，首次把國家主權歸於全國，確立國王與議會分權，並附有涉及宗教與美洲殖民地改革的條款。一八一四年斐迪南七世回國後立即廢止這部憲法，由「使徒派」與極端王黨一派把持朝政，肆行鎮壓，逼走或流放自由派，軍隊與知識界的不滿逐日累積。表面導火線是政府對軍隊的整飭：對軍官榮譽與晉升的干預、對國民警衛隊擴張的警覺，以及宮廷人事的爭鬥，讓炮兵軍官團體尤其反感。真正的引爆點是加的斯的一次即興集會——列戈在除夕夜把駐軍帶出營門，連夜宣布支持舊憲法，等於用一次軍事政變的方式把國家的政治方向強行扭轉。此後的擴散靠的並不是計畫，而是示範效應：每一個願意配合的駐軍都讓另一個猶豫的團體變得不那麼危險，等到馬德里也被拿下，國王就只剩下宣誓一途。此役更深的原因是西班牙在拿破崙戰爭後面臨的國家認同危機：戰時的全民動員、美洲殖民地的獨立與財政的崩潰，使得「舊王朝」與「新國家」之間的裂痕無法再靠行政手段修補。
causeEn: The direct cause was the restoration of King Ferdinand VII after the Peninsular War. During the war a liberal Spain had taken the lead and drawn up the Constitution of 1812, which for the first time placed sovereignty in the nation, divided power between king and Cortes, and included clauses on religion and on reform in the American colonies. When Ferdinand VII returned in 1814 he abolished the Constitution at once; the apostolic and the ultra-royalist party took charge of government, repression followed, liberals were driven out or exiled, and resentment accumulated in the army and in the world of letters. The immediate fuse was the government's disciplining of the army: interference in the honour and the promotion of officers, mistrust of the expansion of the National Guard, and quarrels over court appointments, all of which made the artillery officer corps in particular restive. The real spark was an impromptu gathering of soldiers and officers at Cadiz. Riego marched the garrison out of its barracks on the night of New Year's Eve and proclaimed support for the old Constitution, which amounts to imposing by military coup the new direction of the state. What followed spread less by plan than by example: every garrison that consented made another wavering body seem less dangerous, and once Madrid had fallen, the king had nothing left but to swear the oath. The deeper cause lies in the crisis of national identity that followed the Peninsular War. The mobilisation of the whole population, the independence of the colonies and the collapse of public finance made the rift between the old dynasty and the new nation impossible to repair by administrative means.
impact: 這三年改寫了西班牙的國家形態。就制度而言，一八一二年《加的斯憲法》從此不再是廢紙，自由派把一八二〇至一八二三年的實踐稱為「自由三年期」，並把它視為西班牙近代憲政的第一次成功實驗；雖然一八二三年法軍入城後國王頒下「迪納法令」把這三年的立法一筆勾銷，但自由派並未消失，軍隊中的自由派軍官與知識分子轉入地下，一八三〇年代與一八四八年再度發動，最終在一八六八年逼退伊莎貝拉二世、迎回一八一二年憲法，開啟「六年民主」，也開啟了現代西班牙國家的道路。就歐洲而言，一八二三年的干涉樹立了一個糟糕的先例：法國以干涉之名恢復專制，被維也納會議體系下的歐洲列強視為越界；西西里、那不勒斯、葡萄牙與希臘的自由派因此與西班牙自由派之間形成了一條若隱若現的連線，也讓歐洲輿論對法國的海外用兵多了一層戒心。就軍事而言，一八二三年後西班牙軍隊被大幅裁減與整編，許多曾支持革命的軍官被貶謫或流亡，軍隊的政治中立被打破，這正是日後卡爾派戰爭中軍隊分裂的伏線。就兵器而言，火繩槍這樣的舊式火器在這一役之後加速退場，把位置讓給燧發槍與後來的雷管槍。
impactEn: These three years reshaped the Spanish state. Institutionally, the Constitution of 1812 ceased to be a dead letter: the liberals called the practice of 1820 to 1823 the Liberal Triennium and treated it as the first successful experiment in modern Spanish constitutionalism. Although in 1823 the king's Dina Decrees annulled the legislation of those three years in one stroke, the liberals did not disappear. Liberal officers and intellectuals went underground in the army and the universities, tried again in the 1830s and in 1848, and eventually in 1868 forced Isabella II out and brought the Constitution of 1812 back, opening the Sexenio Democratico and the road to the modern Spanish state. Across Europe, the intervention of 1823 set a bad example: France restoring absolutism in the name of intervention was read by the powers of the Vienna settlement as overreach. A faint line of connection was thus drawn between the liberals of Sicily, Naples, Portugal and Greece and the Spanish liberals, and European opinion grew more wary of French military action abroad. Militarily, after 1823 the Spanish army was cut back and reorganised, many of the officers who had supported the revolution were cashiered or exiled, and the political neutrality of the army was destroyed: that was the fault line along which the army would split again during the Carlist wars. As for weapons, an old arm such as the matchlock was driven further out of service after this campaign, making room for the flintlock and, later, the percussion cap.
result: 結論有三層。第一，這場革命在軍事上成功、在制度上失敗。列戈的一聲宣告讓國王在三個月內失去整個西班牙，也讓一八一二年《加的斯憲法》重新生效三年；制憲議會重開，國王宣誓，攝政制度建立，自由派實際執政。但制度基礎並不牢固：議會與軍隊分裂，國王與王后不甘心受制，政變與反政變接連發生，自由派自己在一八二二年用《皇家法令》換取國王的安全，等於放棄了革命的成果。第二，外來干涉決定了結局。一八二三年春，國王斐迪南七世得以脫離自由派控制，向維也納會議的列強求助，法國波旁王朝以十萬大軍越境而來，自由派陣營在會戰與野戰中都無力對抗。埃斯帕特羅等人在北方的抵抗延續數月，零星的游擊拖慢了法軍推進，但無法扭轉全局：五月二十三日法軍進入馬德里，攝政出逃，議會被解散，制憲派骨幹被逮捕或流亡，一八二三年九月十一日的「迪納法令」把三年立法全部作廢，專制制度重臨西班牙。第三，個人命運成為符號。列戈於同年十一月七日以槍斃執行，屍體不准收葬，成為自由派永久的烈士；托里霍斯後來在馬拉加就義，兩人的名字在十九世紀西班牙革命史上並肩而立。一八二三年之後，西班牙進入十年反動期，直到一八三〇年代自由派的武裝起事才重新出現，並最終在一八六八年開啟通往一九三一年共和國的道路。這場以火繩槍的舊世界殘餘為註腳的革命，最終交出的，是一條通往憲政而非軍閥政治的路。
resultEn: The conclusion has three layers. First, the revolution succeeded militarily and failed institutionally. One declaration by Riego took the whole of Spain from King Ferdinand VII in three months, and the Constitution of 1812 was in force again for three years: the Constituent Cortes reopened, the king took the oath, a regency was created, and the liberals actually governed. But the institutional base was not solid. Cortes and army split apart, king and queen would not submit, coups and counter-coups followed one another, and the liberals themselves exchanged the achievements of the revolution for the king's safety in the Royal Statute of 1822, which amounted to giving up what the revolution had won. Second, foreign intervention decided the ending. In the spring of 1823 King Ferdinand VII, freed from liberal control, appealed to the powers assembled at the Congress of Verona, and the Bourbon monarchy of France crossed the frontier with a hundred thousand men. The liberal camp simply could not stand up to the French in a pitched battle or in the open field. Espartero and others held out in the north for months, and scattered resistance slowed the French advance, but could not turn the course of events: the French entered Madrid on 23 May, the regent fled, the Cortes was dissolved, the leading constitutionalists were arrested or exiled, and the Dina Decrees of 11 September 1823 voided three years of legislation and brought absolutism back to Spain. Third, individual fates became symbols. Riego was shot by a firing squad on 7 November of the same year and was refused burial, becoming the permanent martyr of the liberals; Torrijos was executed in Malaga in 1831, and the two names stand side by side in the nineteenth-century history of the Spanish revolution. After 1823 Spain entered a decade of reaction, and it was not until the 1830s that armed liberal revolts reappeared, eventually opening the road in 1868 that led to the republic of 1931. This revolution, whose footnote was the leftover of the old matchlock world, in the end handed over a road towards constitutional government rather than towards military rule.
